deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is not Dedekind's own mathematics. It is his handwritten copy of a published review (Referat) of E. I. Zolotarev's 1874 Russian thesis on the theory of complex integers. The next page shows this: the quotation closes with '" .....', followed by Dedekind's signed comment of 11 Aug 1876 (he could not obtain the book, and it closely matches his own unpublished first attempts) and a note of 24 Oct 1877 that he borrowed it via A. Wangerin. The underlined phrase at the top ('der Verfasser für eine andere Gelegenheit vor', i.e. the author reserves a case for another occasion) is the passage Dedekind underlined. He took it as evidence that Zolotarev's theory has exceptions.

Setup (modern). Let F(x) in Z[x] be monic of degree n with root x0, and let O_K be the ring of integers of K = Q(x0). Modulo p,
  F ≡ V^m V1^{m1} ... Vs^{ms},
with V, V_i monic irreducible and pairwise distinct mod p. The 'obige Bedingung' (stated on the missing earlier page) is presumably the Kummer/Dedekind regularity condition, i.e. p does not divide the index [O_K : Z[x0]]. Under it, p is declared composite with m prime factors belonging to V, m1 belonging to V1, and so on: p = P^m P1^{m1} ... Ps^{ms}. This is posited independently of whether p actually splits into that many actual complex factors.

Definitions.
- W = V1^{m1}...Vs^{ms}, the cofactor of V^m in F mod p.
- W_i is the analogous cofactor of V_i^{m_i}. The manuscript lists W, W1, ..., Ws.
- phi(x0) = xi_0 + xi_1 x0 + ... + xi_{n-1} x0^{n-1} is any element of Z[x0].

Zolotarev's definition of the P-adic order. Write λ = km + ν with 0 ≤ ν ≤ m-1. Then phi(x0) contains the ideal factor P exactly λ times iff
  (3) phi(x) V^{m-ν} W^{k+1} ≡ 0 mod (p^{k+1}, F(x)) holds, and
  (4) phi(x) V^{2m-ν-1} W^{k+2} ≡ 0 mod (p^{k+2}, F(x)) fails.
Congruence (3) means: the remainder of phi V^{m-ν} W^{k+1} on division by F has degree ≤ n-1 and all coefficients divisible by p^{k+1}. Congruence (4) is read analogously.

Justification (mine, modern). Assume Z[x0] is p-maximal and v_P(V(x0)) = 1. Then:
- v_P(W(x0)) = 0.
- For i ≥ 1, v_{P_i}(W(x0)) ≥ m_i = e_i, so v_{P_i}(W^{k+1}) ≥ v_{P_i}(p^{k+1}). The other primes therefore never obstruct.
- At P, (3) holds iff v_P(phi) + m - ν ≥ (k+1)m, i.e. v_P(phi) ≥ λ.
- At P, (4) holds iff v_P(phi) + 2m - ν - 1 ≥ (k+2)m, i.e. v_P(phi) ≥ λ + 1.
- By p-maximality, divisibility by p^j in O_K agrees with divisibility in Z[x0], hence with the congruence mod (p^j, F).
So (3) and not-(4) is equivalent to v_P(phi) = λ.

The next page says the orders at P_1, ..., P_s are defined the same way, and the whole divisibility theory is derived from this. It mentions the cyclotomic example and the recovery of Kummer's definition. This is a valuation-theoretic ('local') construction of ideal divisors, the approach Dedekind says he himself tried first and abandoned.
errors: No slip in the copied formulas. The exponents in (3) and (4) are consistent and give exactly v_P(phi) = λ.

Unstated hypothesis, perhaps covered by the 'obige Bedingung' on the missing page: one needs v_P(V(x0)) = 1. For m ≥ 2 this follows from Dedekind's criterion. For m = 1 it can fail for a bad choice of lift V; e.g. if v_P(x0 - a) ≥ 2 the test misreports p^k. V must then be adjusted, e.g. V + p.

The method only works when p does not divide the index [O_K : Z[x0]]. This is the exceptional case the reviewer says Zolotarev postpones, and the gap Dedekind underlines and comments on (cf. his Gött. Gel. Anz. 1871 remarks).

results.what: Zolotarev's definition of the exact power of an ideal prime factor P (attached to the factor V^m of F mod p) dividing phi(x0), via the congruences phi V^{m-ν} W^{k+1} ≡ 0 mod (p^{k+1}, F) and the failure of phi V^{2m-ν-1} W^{k+2} ≡ 0 mod (p^{k+2}, F)
results.modern_name: P-adic valuation on a number field; local (valuation-theoretic) construction of divisors; Kummer–Dedekind factorization for p not dividing the index
results.usually_credited_to: E. I. Zolotarev (1874 thesis; 1880 Liouville paper); Kummer for the cyclotomic case; Dedekind (1878) for the Kummer–Dedekind theorem

results.what: Declaring p = P^m P1^{m1}...Ps^{ms} from the factorization of F mod p, under a regularity condition, regardless of whether actual factors exist

deep.surprise_reason: The page is Dedekind's copy of a published review of Zolotarev's thesis, not original work. His interest in Zolotarev, and his view that such congruence-based theories have exceptions (the index-divisor problem), is documented in his published writings and the historical literature (e.g. Edwards). The archival dating of when he obtained the book is a minor detail.

checkable.asserts: Example F=x^2+1, p=2, V=x+1, m=2, W=1, phi=x+1 (λ=1, k=0, ν=1): congruence (3) holds since the remainder is divisible by 2.
Same example: congruence (4) fails since the remainder is not divisible by 4. So v_P(1+i)=1 at P over 2.
F=x^3-2, p=3, F≡(x+1)^3 mod 3, phi=3 (λ=3, k=1, ν=0): congruence (3) holds since every coefficient is divisible by 9.
Same example: congruence (4) fails because 36, 45, 63 are not all divisible by 27. So v_P(3)=3, i.e. 3 is totally ramified.
F=x^2+1, p=5, V=x-2, W=x+2, m=1, phi=x-2 (λ=1, k=1, ν=0): congruence (3) holds modulo 25.
Same: congruence (4) fails since 25x+50 is not divisible by 125. So i-2 has P-valuation exactly 1.

transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'obige Bedingung' is correct; the hand writes something like 'obege', but 'obige' is intended.

The products are W, W1, ..., Ws; the letter that looks like 'N' with a raised dot is a cursive W, also in congruences 3) and 4). The middle example product in the image has a struck-through subscript, corrected to V^m V_2^{m_2}...V_s^{m_s}; the transcription is right.
The marginal '5' beside the phi(x0) formula is the folio number, not an equation label.
'Dedekind IV, 13' is an archival header, not part of the text.
The opening phrase 'der Verfasser für eine andere Gelegenheit vor' is underlined in the original. This is Dedekind's underlining, referred to on the next page.
